language.script_notes: A Baltic language with long-mark (macron) vowels — ā, ē, ī, ū and ō — and the consonants š, ž, č, ģ, ķ, ļ and ņ; many words end in -s or -is. The macron-marked vowels are a quick separator from Estonian and Lithuanian. Russian is widely spoken, especially in Riga.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Thin bollards with a white rectangle on the front and two white circles on the back.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles have curvy, bulbous insulator fittings alternating from side to side. Warning signs have a much thicker red border than those in neighbouring countries, and kilometre markers run parallel to the road. A flagpole near a home or farm is a Latvian habit.

architecture.roof_style: Steep gabled roofs on wooden village houses; flat roofs on Soviet blocks.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal, tile and timber shingle.
architecture.wall_construction: Timber-built vernacular houses, historically made of logs collected from nearby forests, with iconic gabled roofs; Soviet white- and grey-brick blocks three to five storeys tall in village centres; Riga's Art Nouveau and medieval Hanseatic quarters.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Painted timber in muted colours, and grey or white block housing.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Wooden houses with gable ornament; Soviet apartment blocks and cultural houses; Riga's Art Nouveau facades and old town; castles and manor houses in the Gauja valley.

nature.vegetation: Pine and birch forest covers about half the land, with meadows, farmland and peat bogs; sandy pine-fringed beaches along the Baltic.
nature.terrain: Low, flat to gently rolling land with hills reaching only about 300m, many lakes, and a long white-sand Baltic coastline.
nature.climate_signature: Cool, damp and often overcast, with long winters.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and a blue EU strip on the left carrying 'LV'.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of roads and towns.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Neighbouring Baltic language family, flat landscape and similar villages
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bollards here have a white rectangle front and two white circles back, whereas Lithuanian wedge bollards have orange rectangular reflectors; poles here have alternating curvy bulbs; letters ļ, ķ, ņ and macron-marked vowels appear here, while Lithuanian has ė and many -ai and -as endings.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Baltic coast, forests and Soviet blocks
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Estonian uses Õ and its cylindrical bollards and perpendicular kilometre markers differ; warning signs are thicker-bordered here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Soviet blocks, birch forest and timber houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Latin script with macrons and EU plates versus Cyrillic and Russian or Belarusian plates.
